title: Spot Instances: deep discounts, interruptible

kcs.statement: Spot Instances use spare EC2 capacity for up to 90% off On-Demand, but AWS can reclaim them with a two-minute interruption notice.
Spot suits fault-tolerant, flexible, stateless work such as batch jobs, CI builds, big-data processing and rendering, and is the wrong choice for databases or anything that cannot be interrupted.

problem_ideas: A nightly image-rendering job can restart from checkpoints: which purchasing option minimizes cost?
A production MySQL primary on Spot gets a two-minute notice: describe what goes wrong.
On-Demand is $0.20/hour and Spot is $0.05/hour: predict the percentage saving for a 1,000-hour batch run.
A CI system runs hundreds of short test jobs a day: why is Spot a good fit?
Which workload is the distractor for Spot: genomics analysis, web crawling, a payment API, video transcoding?
A team asks for 'cheapest, but must never be interrupted': rule Spot out and name the alternative.
